title: structured output: add constrained decoding backends (CFG/regex) and tokenizer edge-case fixes
author: Alex Chen
description:
Motivation: We need reliable, token-aware constrained decoding for structured-output use cases (CFG/grammar and regex) that work with our runtime batching and streaming model. Existing prototype logic lived as a single post-filter pass and failed on tokenizer edge cases (split punctuation, unicode normalization, and anchor/token boundary issues). This PR introduces two first-class constrained decoding backends (grammar/CFG and regex) integrated with the runtime's token-level scoring pipeline, plus a set of tokenizer fixes and E2E tests.

Summary of changes: implement a grammar-based backend that performs constraint validation during decoding (early accept/reject) using a compact state machine derived from CFG productions; implement a tokenizer-aware regex backend that matches against token sequences rather than raw bytes to avoid accidental matches across token boundaries; add canonicalization utilities for common tokenizer quirks (unicode normalization, punctuation splitting); expose constraint violation semantics in the OpenAI-compat layer (clear error codes and partial-output handling); add metrics and tracing hooks for constraint checks to the Redwood Console; add unit and E2E tests covering tokenizer edge cases and streaming scenarios; update docs and examples.

Design notes: - Grammar backend: we compile a restricted CFG subset into a deterministic parser state machine optimized for left-to-right incremental validation. The parser supports required tokens, optional groups, and simple repetition (no full Turing-power grammars) to keep runtime complexity predictable. On each token, the grammar backend advances states and returns whether the path is still viable, whether the token completes a required symbol, and whether a terminal has been reached.
- Regex backend: regex constraints are applied at token granularity. We precompile regexes into a per-token-state automaton that is aware of token boundaries (anchor handling like ^/$ anchored to token sequence start/end). For character-level regexes that require crossing token boundaries, the backend will optionally switch to a fallback mode that performs a limited lookback on raw text with a cap to maintain latency SLOs.
- Tokenizer edge-cases: multiple fixes: canonicalize NFC/NFD, normalize various quote/dash variants, handle trailing punctuation tokens (",") correctly in anchor matching, and ensure logit_bias mapping remains aligned with token IDs after normalization. We added a tokenizer utility that maps character spans to token index spans to support accurate regex matching and error reporting.

Compatibility and API: - OpenAI-compat layer now accepts a new `constraints` field (array of constraint objects with type: "grammar" | "regex", and backend options). Errors surface as structured error objects with codes: CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION, BACKEND_TIMEOUT, TOKENIZER_MISMATCH. Partial outputs emitted during streaming when a constraint causes early termination are labeled with `constraint_truncated: true` in the response metadata. - Backends are swappable: runtime config accepts `constraint_backend_preference` and per-request override to choose grammar-first or regex-first.

Testing & rollout: added unit tests for grammar parsing edge cases and regex-token matching. Added E2E tests that spin up a lightweight model shim to exercise streaming interactions and ensure no out-of-order constraint checks under batching. Initial rollout gated behind a feature flag `constrained_decoding_v2` and will be enabled for a subset of internal customers for two weeks before broader enablement.

Performance: microbenchmarks show ~2.8% median token cost increase for grammar checks in the pessimistic path, and <1% for common regex constraints using the token-aware automaton. We added new metrics to track constraint checks per-token and constraint-induced latency p95.

Migration notes: existing constraint payloads in the old post-filter format will be migrated server-side to the new representation; clients using advanced regex relying on raw bytes should review the new tokenizer-aware semantics and may opt into `raw_byte_mode` when necessary.

References: ENG-5342 (design doc), ENG-5401 (benchmark plan), SUP-221 (customer-reported tokenizer failure).

review_comments: Priya Nair (2026-02-11): Design LGTM overall. Please add a metric to count constraint-induced backtracks and an opt-in flag for raw_byte_mode. Also can we add a small note about complexity guarantees in the docs?
Alex Chen (2026-02-11): Thanks Priya — added backtrack_count metric and a per-request `raw_byte_mode` toggle; updated docs with complexity note (see last commit).

Miguel Santos (2026-02-12): I saw a potential streaming race where partial outputs might be emitted before constraint checks complete under heavy batching. Can you add an integration test and ensure we stall token emission while validation is pending?

Alex Chen (2026-02-12): Added a streaming alignment check in e2e tests and introduced a small per-request stall window (configurable) to wait for backend validation when needed. This keeps latency within SLOs in practice.
Emma Zhou (2026-02-14): Minor nit: doc example JSON uses old post-filter key. Please update example to use the new `constraints` schema. Otherwise approved.
Alex Chen (2026-02-14): Updated example in docs. Thanks Emma!
Miguel Santos (2026-02-16): Verified performance numbers on internal canary; the p95 stays within target when grammar backend is used with optimistic caching. Approving to merge.
release_notes: Adds first-class constrained decoding backends: grammar (CFG subset) and tokenizer-aware regex. Fixes tokenizer normalization and anchor handling for constraints. Exposes a `constraints` field in the OpenAI-compat API with structured error codes. Feature gated behind `constrained_decoding_v2`.
